solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spurt of speed not quite restrained by untidy cable, road hazard?

indicators.note: something restrained by another is held within it, so one piece sits inside the other
an untidy cable is tangled, so its letters are rearranged
not quite the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a kick is a sudden burst of pace, as from a runner near the finish

explanation.surface: A runner's sprint is hampered by a messy cable — a trip hazard on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spurt of speed' reads like part of the surface story, but it is the kick a runner finds near the finish, trimmed by 'not quite'.
explanation.definitionFit: Invisible frozen film on tarmac is a classic danger to drivers; the question mark admits it is one hazard among many.

clue.text: Stick material made by a doctor in reserve mostly

indicators.note: the a and doctor letters go inside the shortened reserve word
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: to book is to reserve
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: Material for canes produced by a medic held in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts BOOK to BOO; A and MB go 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bamboo is the woody grass from which canes and poles are made, a material for sticks.

clue.text: Number making way for duke in secret place of amusement

indicators.note: one letter steps aside so another can take its place

parts.note: arcane means secret, known only to a few

explanation.surface: A figure steps aside so a nobleman can enter a hidden playground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making way for' swaps the N of ARCANE for D.
explanation.definitionFit: An amusement arcade houses slot machines and video games, a place for fun.

clue.text: A trek planned to take in a martial sport

indicators.note: to take in is to enclose, so one letter goes inside the rest
a planned trek is arranged, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hike is organised to include a combat sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planned' rearranges A TREK into KARTE, which takes in the second A.
explanation.definitionFit: Karate is a Japanese unarmed combat discipline, one of the martial arts practised as sport.

clue.text: Fellow replacing note in link? That's sweet

indicators.note: one letter takes the place of another in the word

parts.note: a connection is a link
n. is an abbreviation for note, as in a footnote

explanation.surface: Swapping a man for a musical note in a chain makes something lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' is N here, the abbreviation used for a footnote, not a musical letter; 'replacing' swaps the second N of CONNECTION for F.
explanation.definitionFit: A confection is a sugary delicacy, a candy, so it is a synonym of the noun sweet.

clue.text: Coolness shown by a revolutionary agent without European in lead

indicators.note: the agent piece is placed inside the symbol for lead

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead

indicators.note: a revolutionary turns things round, so the word is read backwards
the agent's word is taken without the letter for European

parts.note: a mole is a spy, an agent planted in an organisation

explanation.surface: Composure displayed by a spy who has left Europe and gone into lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops E from MOLE to leave MOL; 'revolutionary' turns that to LOM, which goes 'in' PB.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplomb is self-assured composure, a synonym for coolness under pressure.

clue.text: Chap's tie in a mess? It's made of hybrid material

indicators.note: a tie in a mess is jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man's necktie is messy — it is made of mixed fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'Chap's' counts as a letter of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche is a work assembled from borrowed styles and fragments, a medley of mixed sources.

clue.text: Deliveries before eating area reportedly getting thorough examination

indicators.note: the cricket word comes before the rest in the answer

parts.note: an over is a set of six deliveries (balls) in cricket

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: a hall is a dining hall, a college or school eating area

explanation.surface: Balls bowled before a canteen is inspected thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled from one end. HALL said aloud gives HAUL.
explanation.definitionFit: An overhaul is a complete inspection and repair, a synonym for a thorough examination.

clue.text: Person receiving expression of sympathy in a state of worry

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: bod is informal British for a person
'there, there' is said to comfort someone, so there expresses sympathy

explanation.surface: Someone getting a few comforting words because they are anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Bothered means troubled or anxious, an adjective matching the phrase describing worry.

clue.text: A lot of enthusiasm about a recipe in company making pasta

indicators.note: the shortened enthusiasm word goes around the rest
a lot of a word but not all of it, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a mania is a wild enthusiasm or craze

indicators.note: the a and recipe letters go inside the company abbreviation

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe (Latin 'take'), seen on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Great eagerness for a dish leads a firm to produce pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' trims MANIA to MANI; A and R go 'in' CO to give CARO; MANI goes 'about' CARO.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroni is a type of pasta in short tubes, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Bearing or not bearing children protected by a city teacher originally

indicators.note: something protected by others is enclosed by them, so it sits inside

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
s.p. (sine prole, Latin 'without issue') is the genealogists' abbreviation for dying childless

indicators.note: originally means the word's first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A puzzling question whether a teacher in the city has or hasn't had children.
explanation.walkthrough: s.p. comes from the Latin sine prole used in family trees; the City of London's postcode is EC. 'Bearing' then repeats in the wordplay, a teasing echo.
explanation.definitionFit: One's aspect is one's appearance or demeanour, the way one carries oneself, which is a synonym of bearing.

clue.text: Recall celebration with timeless songs and singular characteristics

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the word for celebration is read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: timeless means without a T, the abbreviation for time

parts.note: ditties are simple songs

explanation.surface: Remembering a party with old songs and some peculiar traits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recall' reverses DO to OD; 'timeless' takes a T from DITTIES, leaving DITIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddities are peculiar traits or quirks, matching singular in its sense of strange or unusual.

clue.text: Story about Chinese beginning to export fruit

indicators.note: the story word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story

indicators.note: beginning to a word means its first letter

explanation.surface: A tale concerning Chinese starting to send fruit abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The lichee, more often spelt lychee, is a small sweet Chinese fruit, an example of the category.

clue.text: Hot state mostly with a Republican in trouble? Take pity

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly

indicators.note: the Republican letter goes inside the trouble word

parts.note: heat is pressure or trouble, as in 'the heat is on'

explanation.surface: A sweltering state, with a Republican in difficulty, pleads for mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' is a verb here, AVER, which 'mostly' trims to AVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a plea for compassion: show mercy and be kind, much like taking pity.

clue.text: Take amiss hotel in pickle — and specialist restaurant

indicators.note: the shuffled word and hotel go inside the pickle word

parts.note: to souse is to pickle in brine or vinegar; as a noun, a souse is pickle

indicators.note: taken amiss, the letters go wrong and are rearranged

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Taking offence at a hotel in a mess — and at a specialist restaurant too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amiss' rearranges TAKE to TEAK; TEAK and H go 'in' SOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A steakhouse is an eatery that concentrates on grilled beef, so it is a restaurant with a speciality.

clue.text: Worthless training area by the sound of it supported by expert

indicators.note: in a down clue the expert word sits beneath and so supports the first piece
the training area word is heard rather than read, giving its sound

parts.note: a gym is a place for physical training
crack means first-rate or expert, as in a crack shot

explanation.surface: A useless gym, it seems, propped up by a specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: Gimcrack describes showy but flimsy and cheap goods, so it is a synonym for worthless.

clue.text: Eastern Italian circling river? Ancient one

indicators.note: the Italian word goes round the river letter

parts.note: a Tuscan is an Italian from Tuscany

explanation.surface: An Italian from the east going round a river is an old one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Etruscans were a pre-Roman people of central Italy, so one of them is an ancient person.

clue.text: Criticise Democrat's opening part of speech in European church

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
the part of speech goes inside the European and church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a noun is a part of speech

explanation.surface: A Democrat begins a speech section in a European church condemning something.
explanation.definitionFit: To denounce is to condemn publicly, a strong synonym for criticise.

clue.text: Loaded container opening at last with delightful stuff enthralling English male

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is moved to the end

parts.note: a tin is a container

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the other letters sit inside

parts.note: honey is sweet stuff, figuratively anything delightful

explanation.surface: A can full of something sweet captivates an English gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening at last' means the container's first letter goes to the end; 'Loaded' looks like 'full' but means rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded is slang for rich, as is the idiom of being well supplied with cash.

clue.text: Jag largely carrying man in field of activity

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so one piece goes inside the other
largely means most but not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a jag is a bout of indulgence, a spree
he is a male person

explanation.surface: A Jaguar car mostly holds a man on a sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jag' looks like the car; it is a drinking bout, SPREE, which 'largely' cuts to SPRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere is a domain or area of interest, as in one's sphere of influence.

clue.text: Companion amid calm cut food

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so one piece goes inside
cut means the end letter is chopped off

parts.note: quiet means calm
CH is a Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A friend among peace reduces food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' shortens QUIET to QUIE; CH, the Companion of Honour (a British award), goes 'amid' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiche is a savoury egg tart, an example of a dish to eat.

clue.text: Go round grubby passenger? Not altogether

indicators.note: Not altogether says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dirty traveller? Not completely.
explanation.definitionFit: To bypass is to avoid by taking a route around, as a ring road skirts a town.

clue.text: Ticket giving rebels a quick go-ahead?

parts.note: a coup is a quick seizure of power by rebels
on means go, as in 'the deal is on'

explanation.surface: A voucher that allows insurgents a speedy approval.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupon is a slip entitling the holder to something, a voucher or ticket.

clue.text: College trips before an about-turn for exotic fare

indicators.note: the first pieces come before the about-turn in the answer

parts.note: hops are short journeys or trips
a U-ey (or uey) is informal, chiefly Australian, for a U-turn

explanation.surface: Student journeys precede a change of heart over foreign food.
explanation.definitionFit: Chop suey is a Chinese-American stir-fry, an unfamiliar dish to Western diners and so foreign food.

clue.text: Report of dismissal conveyed stress

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the phrase is said aloud

parts.note: axe means dismissal and sent means conveyed, the two together making axe sent

explanation.surface: News of a sacking carried real emphasis.
explanation.definitionFit: In speech an accent is the emphasis placed on a syllable, a synonym of stress.

clue.text: Senior facilities held back around cold European city

indicators.note: the reversed pieces wrap around the cold letter
held back means taken backwards, so the pieces read in reverse

parts.note: aîné is French for elder or senior
lav, short for lavatory, is a convenience or facilities
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Pensioners' amenities are delayed in a chilly continental city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Senior' needs French: aîné, the elder; 'held back' reverses both pieces together before 'around' wraps them round the cold letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Valencia is a large port city on Spain's eastern coast, an example of a European city.

clue.text: Barge round sides of northern home of Dane?

indicators.note: the barge word goes round the other letters

parts.note: a keel is a flat-bottomed boat used on the Tyne, a barge

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A boat circling the edge of a northern home of a Scandinavian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dane' misleads towards Denmark; it is the Great Dane, a dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A kennel is a dog's shelter, and a Great Dane is a dog, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Priest set off ignoring independent church of note

indicators.note: set off means disturbed, so the letters are rearranged
ignoring means one letter of the pool is left out of the new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cleric sets out, paying no heed to a famous church nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' shuffles PRIEST SET, and 'ignoring' drops the I for independent from the pool before it is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: St Peter's in Rome is a famous basilica, a notable church.
